ranked.headline: Attention and graph models advance drug-target and binding affinity prediction
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and papers fuse graph, sequence, and attention models to predict drug-target, protein-protein, and microbe-drug interactions.

ranked.headline: Pathology foundation models extend to multi-omics alignment and fairness-aware adaptation
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and publications pair histology foundation models with transcriptomic, genomic, and spatial omics data, broadening their scope beyond…

ranked.headline: Computational corrections for technical variation across transcriptomic and epigenomic…
ranked.summary: Multi-omic and spatial datasets make batch, segmentation and reference choices consequential, driving quantitative benchmarking of these methods.

ranked.headline: Joint antigen quality, HLA context and off-target risk in neoantigen prioritization
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and one glioma study show neoantigen scores increasingly combine sequencing, HLA evolution and population-aware off-target risk.

ranked.headline: Genome-resolved units define microbial and algal lineage boundaries and traits
ranked.summary: Isolate, metagenome-derived, and single-genome resources now resolve lineage boundaries and trait distributions across microbes and algae.

ranked.headline: Multiscale self-supervised models learn scale-aware representations of neural dynamics
ranked.summary: Recent preprints treat spatial and temporal scale as a modeling variable across fMRI, iEEG, spike, and LFP recordings.

ranked.headline: Probing where structure prediction, simulation and free-energy methods stay trustworthy
ranked.summary: Recent benchmarks of structure predictors on nanobody-small molecule complexes, plus new sampling and simulation methods, test where models remain reliable.

ranked.headline: Single-cell and sample-level models map disease and developmental states to cell types
ranked.summary: Population-scale single-cell data now localize regulatory, communication and drug-response effects to specific cell states across disease cohorts.

ranked.headline: Comparative genomics links selection, lifestyle and gene content across diverse lineages
ranked.summary: Expanded genome sets now let comparative analyses attribute gene content, codon usage and repeat patterns to selection, transmission or lifestyle.

ranked.headline: Compartmental models link behavioral, vector and spillover risk to transmission
ranked.summary: Transmission models now address behavioral feedback, arbovirus control and pandemic potential, each tied to intervention or surveillance decisions.

ranked.headline: Multi-omics and graph models predict BRAF inhibitor response in cancer cell lines
ranked.summary: Multi-omics fusion, protein network embeddings and explainable GNNs are extending drug response models to cell lines, tissues and checkpoint therapy.

ranked.headline: Embeddings coupled to literature retrieval for omics and disease hypothesis generation
ranked.summary: Recent preprints couple learned omics representations with literature retrieval and LLM-based interpretation, with performance self-reported.

ranked.headline: Open tools extend 3D structure analysis to glycans, multimers, and molecular ensembles
ranked.summary: Structure-aware software now spans glycans, protein complexes, and MD ensembles, enabling evolutionary and interaction analyses from 3D coordinates.

ranked.headline: Quantitative representations infer single-cell behavior and lineage from imaging data
ranked.summary: Recent items state geometric representation and lineage-spatial coupling explicitly within single-cell inference, from graph models to tracking infrastructure.

ranked.headline: Mechanistic models forecast treatment response dynamics from sparse or lineage data
ranked.summary: Mechanistic models are being fit to sparse data to infer time-varying treatment effects and chemotherapy-induced cell cycle dynamics.

ranked.headline: Pooled Cell Painting and spatial barcoding resolve gene function at single-cell scale
ranked.summary: Recent work pairs multiplexed imaging, network metrics, and barcoding to link single-cell perturbations to gene function and clonal fate.

ranked.headline: Modeling missingness and platform effects in methylation and genotype data at scale
ranked.summary: Biobank-scale studies combining methylation and genotyping arrays now require explicit handling of platform differences and missing values.

ranked.headline: Pretrained sequence models supply features for narrow biological prediction tasks
ranked.summary: Pretrained protein and glycan representations are being paired with narrow predictors for ion channels, gene cluster products, and glycans.

ranked.headline: Quality-audited genome references underpin reliable phylogenomic and mitogenome inference
ranked.summary: Expanding public genome collections demand reliability audits before comparative inference, as three preprints on fungal, viral and nematode data illustrate.

ranked.headline: Biophysical models link axon geometry and stimulation physics to neural function
ranked.summary: Resolved geometry and stimulation physics now enable quantitative predictions of conduction and membrane potential in neural models.

ranked.headline: Machine learning on multi-omics data predicts drug response, survival and ER binding
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and a published study apply predictive and survival modeling to single-cell and bulk multi-omics to stratify patients and drug responders.

ranked.headline: Structure and synthesis constraints guide generative design of binders and degraders
ranked.summary: Pipelines now treat synthesizability and small-molecule antigen sites as explicit constraints alongside structural models.

ranked.headline: Genome-scale models map bacterial metabolism across strains, conditions and consortia
ranked.summary: Population-scale genome sets now pair with transcriptomic context, letting metabolic models scale to 7,835 Klebsiella genomes.

ranked.headline: Learning-enhanced virtual screening yields helicase and PLK2 inhibitor candidates
ranked.summary: Iterative deep learning and consensus interaction models are improving virtual screening hit identification for SARS-CoV-2 and PLK2 targets.

ranked.headline: Caller choice and classification models shape variant-level inference accuracy
ranked.summary: Variant calling and classification choices now propagate into mutational signature inference, ctDNA detection, and ACMG germline interpretation.

ranked.headline: Reduced and spatial models of structured cellular and microbial interactions
ranked.summary: Explicit interaction structure and cross-scale coupling keep multicellular, microbial, and infection models mechanistically tractable.

ranked.headline: Uncertainty and observation quality are being built into single-cell analysis methods
ranked.summary: Single-cell and coexpression analyses increasingly must account for sparse observation and network variability to yield reliable inferences.

ranked.headline: Nonadditive genetic effects and causal protein networks validated across cohorts
ranked.summary: Large biobank and cohort studies now test non-additive and causal genetic architecture, with replication across proteomic platforms and populations.

ranked.headline: Algorithms enumerate structured paths and blocks in graph and genealogical sequence data
ranked.summary: Combinatorial formulations with stated complexity are emerging for path and block inference across graph, genealogical, and synteny representations.

ranked.headline: Excitatory-inhibitory structure constrains the dynamics recurrent networks can express
ranked.summary: Spectral theory, Dale's-law training, and human imaging of an LSD-induced E/I shift now converge on how E/I structure shapes network dynamics.

ranked.headline: Spatial methylome, imaging, and transcriptomic profiling resolve tissue cell states
ranked.summary: Spatial methods now pair near single-cell methylation and imaging mass cytometry with poly(A)-aware atlases to map tissue cell states in situ.

ranked.headline: Integrating contact maps and epigenomic profiles to infer genome regulatory architecture
ranked.summary: Single-cell and contact-mapping datasets now resolve factor binding order, RNA-DNA contacts, and 4D nucleome structure in human cells.

ranked.headline: Genome-scale models guide growth media design; ML predicts enzyme kinetic parameters
ranked.summary: Constraint-based media optimization, ML prediction of enzyme kinetics, and a strain design literature database each target metabolic engineering decisions.

ranked.headline: Open-source tools formalize interval, microhaplotype, and chromatin data operations
ranked.summary: Recent preprints package recurring single-cell, sequencing, and genomic interval operations into shareable standards, pipelines, and interactive interfaces.

ranked.headline: Sequence-resolved telomeres and centromeres reveal reproducible chromosomal architecture
ranked.summary: Nanopore and T2T pedigree assemblies now resolve telomeres, centromeres and rDNA across individuals, tissues and generations.

ranked.headline: Reference-free inference for peptide and proteoform identification from mass spectra
ranked.summary: Predictive modeling and statistical inference are coupled to higher-throughput acquisition and reference construction in MS proteomics.

ranked.headline: Structure-based models constrain RNA-protein and nucleic acid quadruplex conformations
ranked.summary: Explicit structural specification now links nucleic acid sequence, flexibility, and folding to predictive conformational models.

ranked.headline: Genomic AMR prediction errors trace to thresholds, population structure, and sampling
ranked.summary: Recent work traces AMR prediction error to reference cutoffs and sampling design as nanopore sequencing reaches blood cultures within hours.

ranked.headline: Alternative splicing and NMD efficiency examined across tumors, GTEx and glioma atlases
ranked.summary: Per-sample NMD efficiency metrics and large GTEx and single-cell resources now enable splicing variation to be quantified across tumors and normal tissue.
